\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مول} (mawwala)}{مول (mawwala)}]{\ar{مول} (mawwala) — to fund}

\label{lesson:AR-C384-mawwala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for inflation, then the Arabic for to invest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مول}}
\textbf{\ar{مول}} — \emph{mawwala} — \textquotedblleft{}to fund\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{مولت} \ar{الدولة} \ar{المشروع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mawwalat ad-dawla al-mashrūʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The state funded the project.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يمول}, \emph{yumawwil}.

The noun \ar{تمويل}, \emph{tamwīl}, funding.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مول}} (\emph{mawwala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-w-l}, \textquotedblleft{}wealth, property\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II of the root of \emph{māl}, money: to provide with money, to fund.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mawwala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mawwala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mawwalat ad-dawla al-mashrūʿ.} — The state funded the project.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for inflation, then the Arabic for to invest, then say \emph{mawwala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مول} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To fund\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{خصص} (khaṣṣaṣa)}{خصص (khaṣṣaṣa)}]{\ar{خصص} (khaṣṣaṣa) — to allocate}

\label{lesson:AR-C384-khassasa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to invest, then the Arabic for to fund.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{خصص}}
\textbf{\ar{خصص}} — \emph{khaṣṣaṣa} — \textquotedblleft{}to allocate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{خصصت} \ar{المدرسة} \ar{غرفة} \ar{للموسيقى}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khaṣṣaṣat al-madrasa ghurfa li-l-mūsīqā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The school set aside a room for music.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يخصص}, \emph{yukhaṣṣiṣ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{خصص}} (\emph{khaṣṣaṣa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-ṣ-ṣ}, \textquotedblleft{}to single out\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, to single out for one purpose: to allocate, to set aside.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صناعة} (ṣināʿa)}{صناعة (ṣināʿa)}]{\ar{صناعة} (ṣināʿa) — industry}

\label{lesson:AR-C384-sinaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to fund, then the Arabic for to allocate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صناعة}}
\textbf{\ar{صناعة}} — \emph{ṣināʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}industry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{صناعة} \ar{السيارات} \ar{كبيرة} \ar{في} \ar{هذا} \ar{البلد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṣināʿat as-sayyārāt kabīra fī hādhā al-balad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The car industry is big in this country.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صناعة}} (\emph{ṣināʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-n-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to make, to manufacture\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ṣināʿa} is a craft, the work of making: industry.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{زراعة} (zirāʿa)}{زراعة (zirāʿa)}]{\ar{زراعة} (zirāʿa) — agriculture}

\label{lesson:AR-C384-ziraa}

Before the new one: say the Arabic for to allocate, then the Arabic for industry.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تنمية} (tanmiya)}{تنمية (tanmiya)}]{\ar{تنمية} (tanmiya) — development}

\label{lesson:AR-C384-tanmiya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for industry, then the Arabic for agriculture.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تنمية}}
\textbf{\ar{تنمية}} — \emph{tanmiya} — \textquotedblleft{}development\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تحتاج} \ar{القرية} \ar{إلى} \ar{تنمية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taḥtāju al-qarya ilā tanmiya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The village needs development.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تنمية}} (\emph{tanmiya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-m-w}, usually traced to the sense \textquotedblleft{}to grow, to increase\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Tanmiya} is the Form II verbal noun, making a thing grow: development.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}
